label: Formaggio di fossa
note: Rarely buffalo milk too; matured 20-30 days before burying per Wikipedia (the PDO rules are reported as at least 80 days, sources differ)

about.text: Formaggio di fossa (pit cheese) comes from Sogliano al Rubicone in Emilia-Romagna, where cheese has been buried in pits dug in tufa since the 14th century. Cheese sold as fossa di Sogliano has had protected designation of origin status since 2009.

sources.text: The first paragraph of its article, shortened.
The photograph, its author and its licence, from its page.

how.label: bury in tufa pits
how.text: The cheese is not made differently from other semi-hard cheeses; it is ripened in a sealed pit, and the pit itself is part of the recipe.

steps.note: Matured 20-30 days before burying, though the PDO rules are reported as at least 80 days.

steps.name: prepare pit
steps.note: Straw is burned in it to dry and sanitise it, and walls and floor are lined with straw, reeds and planks.

steps.name: bag
steps.note: The wheels go into white cotton or linen bags, about ten per bag.

steps.name: bury
steps.note: Buried in mid-to-late August and sealed in with plaster, wood and sand.
Without air the fermentation is anaerobic, and the cheese softens and loses lactose, water and fat.

steps.name: unearth
steps.note: On St Catherine (25 Nov) in Sogliano, St Martin (11 Nov) in Perticara.
